content: Figure FIGREF51 shows the average dominance of each group label's word2vec representation's 1000 nearest neighbors according to the NRC VAD Dominance Lexicon BIBREF56, which we use as an estimate of the dominance associated with each group label. American is clearly significantly associated with greater dominance than gay, homosexual, and all LGBTQ terms (Wilcoxon signed-rank test; $p < 0.0001$), and gay has significantly higher dominance than homosexual ($p < 0.0001$). While the dominance associated with gay and all LGBTQ terms significantly increased over the three decades ($p < 0.01$), dominance significantly decreased for homosexual ($p < 0.0001$). Furthermore, while the increase in average nearest neighbor dominance does not reach significance for gay and all LGBTQ terms in the most recent 15 years ($p = 0.47$ for all LGBTQ terms and $p = 0.066$ for gay), homosexual significantly decreases in that time span ($p < 0.0001$).
